item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the patch I would rather review and merge, although it still needs correction before merging.","reasons":["A adds the exact Upload signature, uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and verifies filename, content, and replay across both retry attempts.","A keeps option handling, request construction, response decoding, and errors centralized in a shared add helper, whereas B duplicates the existing Add implementation inside Upload.","B explicitly violates scope by adding WithFilesFormFields and association-field machinery, which the contract forbids.","B also refactors global request/retry behavior and changes Raw.Do reader-ownership semantics, despite the contract explicitly excluding unrelated retry changes and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the private add helper rather than routing through the public Add method as explicitly required.","Add now eagerly reads and buffers every caller-built body, changing the preserved lower-level API's streaming and error behavior.","The added tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Upload does not route through Add and instead duplicates its request and response logic.","It adds forbidden association fields and changes FilesOption behavior.","It introduces broad retry machinery and a caller-ownership change for seekable bodies outside the requested scope; the shared mutable seeker also makes replay handling more fragile and seek-to-end failure may leave position handling ambiguousive? Actually invalid word. Need correct JSON." ]}
